newsitem.title: UK: World oil prices drift down but firmer over week.
newsitem.headline: World oil prices drift down but firmer over week.

text.p: World oil prices on Friday were around a dollar higher than at the start of the week, but ebbed from the highs of the day.
At 1653 GMT, London March futures for international benchmark crude oil Brent blend fell 31 cents to trade at $22.87 a barrel.
Traders said the market was consolidating after a bounce back up from the $22 low seen on Monday.
"I don't think we've really cracked any levels, but I don't see it as a reversal of the trend either," said Leslie Nicholas, energy analyst at GNI in London.
Analysts said weaker heating oil in the United States helped to drive prices down on Friday.
Milder weather there dampened demand fro heating oil, pulling down crude in its wake.
"At this time of year heating oil is prone to selling into the rallies rather than buying through," Nicholas said.
Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp predicted near normal to just above normal temperatures for Friday and Saturday in the northeast of the United States, the world's largest heating market.
No major cold was anticipated in Northwest Europe.
